summary: Modoc NF steel tower completed October 1929; 1962 steel house replaced the cab on the existing tower; still listed standing and staffed in fire season.

facts.design: Forest Service steel lookout tower (Region 5 4AR design, 1929); 14-foot-square glass cab; 1962 steel CL-100 house on the existing tower
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Modoc National Forest

events.note: First steel lookout tower in Modoc National Forest, completed October 1929
Ed H. Stuart occupied the lookout during the 1929 season
Gilbert Busch lookout man until late October
Gilbert W. Busch stationed on the peak for the summer
Two tent cabins erected beside the tower for the lookout man's family
Lookout made 20 first discoveries during 1942 through 1946
Orville and Genelle Stevens assigned as lookout fireman and primary lookout
New outside stairway replaced the trapdoor entrance through the cab floor
New steel lookout house (CL-100) built on the existing tower for $20,314, completed October 1962

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give the original tower as 20 feet (September 1929 newspaper and NHLR), 22 feet (October 1929 newspapers) and 25 feet (1931 newspaper). The record's height_m of 7.6 (25 ft) matches only the 1931 report, so height is left out of facts pending editor choice.

The NHLR dates the original structure to October 1929, and a 1963 newspaper says the house it replaced was built in 1931. The story keeps 1929 for the tower and reports the house dates as conflicting.

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 7.6 (25 ft) is supported only by the 1931 report; NHLR says 20 ft and the October 1929 papers say 22 ft. I left height out of facts for your choice. The 1962 house is a rebuild on the existing tower and was not in the brief's events, so I added it as 'replaced'. The NHLR staffing line is undated; as_of is the date I read it. The NHLR's 1929 date and the 1963 newspaper's 1931 date conflict; the story says so. FLO also lists a separate tree lookout, Blue Mountain Tree (East Peak), that this record does not cover. No rental or access notice was found, so there is no access or visit block.
